outOfScope: Migrating, deleting or cutting over any current unfinished legacy Blackboard task.
Rewriting DONE task history or Living Docs.
constraints: Task 1 builds the new control plane only. It must not migrate or cut over any current unfinished legacy work.
Blackboard authority must be readable identically from any checkout/worktree and must not depend on whichever source branch is currently checked out.
A new Work must be creatable directly in the control plane before any source PR or branch exists.
Context is derived output, not authority: no context generation/history/currentContextRef persistence in the V2 model.
Source branches, worktrees and candidate SHAs are attempt bindings only and never become Blackboard truth.
Independent Jev judgment, exact candidate/evidence/merge binding, negative-case verification and Living Docs delivery truth remain trust primitives; V2 may adapt them but must not weaken them.
The lifecycle and legal next actions must be executable state-machine data/code; operator docs may explain semantics but cannot be required to infer what action is legal next.
invariants: Exactly one V2 control authority owns a Work's semantic/lifecycle state; source branches and worktrees cannot override it.
Work creation and research entry do not require a source-code commit or PR.
Context is always derived from Work + current system truth + exact decisions/attempt bindings and is never persisted as authority.
Every state transition is explicit, guarded and enumerable; no operator or agent infers lifecycle from prose.
Jev/evidence/delivery decisions remain external trusted receipts bound back to the exact Work generation and Attempt.
Lease expiry and takeover safety are decided only from the ControlStore's authoritative clock; agent-provided time is never used for lease validity, expiry or takeover.

Decision publication is a compare-and-swap mutation: a decision applies only when its observedGeneration exactly equals the current Work spec.generation at publish time; otherwise it is recorded/returned as SUPERSEDED and cannot mutate status or phase.

nextActions(work) is a pure deterministic function of the canonical `(spec, status, decisions)` snapshot. Given byte-equivalent inputs, independent controllers must compute byte-equivalent next actions, blockers and forbidden actions.

Fence validation is required only on mutating side effects owned by an Attempt—candidate/evidence publication and lifecycle/status transitions. Read-only inspection and context building never require a fence.
architectureDecisions: D1 — Introduce an isolated V2 control-plane module under scripts/blackboard-v2/**. Task 1 does not mutate legacy work-graph/artifact lifecycle beyond registering this task. The V2 module can coexist with legacy until BB-156 cutover.

D2 — Store V2 authority behind a BlackboardControlStore abstraction. The production implementation uses a dedicated Git control ref (preferred `refs/exharness/blackboard`) whose tree contains one Work resource per id plus allocation metadata. Every mutation uses compare-and-swap against the current resourceVersion. The ControlStore owns the authoritative clock used for leases; agent clocks/timestamps are informational only and can never decide expiry or takeover.

D3 — Define WORK_RESOURCE_V2 as `{id,generation,spec,status}`. `spec` owns objective, current plan, dependencies and components. `status` owns lifecycle phase, conditions, activeAttempt and observedGeneration bindings. Updating semantic desired state increments generation; judgments/conditions bind the generation they observed.

D4 — Define an executable lifecycle table/function as the only source of legal transitions. Minimum phases: PROPOSED, RESEARCHING, PLAN_JUDGMENT, READY, EXECUTING, JUDGING, REPAIRING, MERGE_PENDING, DELIVERED, BLOCKED. `nextActions(work)` is pure/deterministic over the canonical `(spec,status,decisions)` snapshot and performs no I/O, clock reads or mutation. Guards consume only explicit snapshot facts; docs are descriptive only.

D5 — `nextActions(work)` returns bounded machine-readable actions with required inputs/blockers/forbidden actions. The CLI `bb-v2 next <id>` renders that result; `show` renders canonical Work state; `create` atomically allocates/publishes a new Work without touching a source branch.

D6 — `buildContext(work)` is a pure projection from canonical Work, component/current-system routing and the lifecycle's next-action contract. It returns goal, input refs/subjects, read/write scope, forbidden actions and required output. It has no generation, parent context, currentContextRef or persisted context file.

D7 — Source work is represented by ATTEMPT_V2 bound to `{workId,workGeneration,baseSha,sourceRef?,candidateSha?,owner,leaseUntil,fence}`. Claim/takeover is a ControlStore CAS using the store clock; exactly one active attempt wins. Fence checks are enforced only on mutating Attempt side effects (candidate/evidence publication and lifecycle/status transitions), not reads. Jev readiness/candidate evaluations and delivery receipts are immutable decisions/receipts bound to exact workGeneration and attempt/candidate identity.

D8 — Task 1 proves branch independence and lifecycle usability with new synthetic V2 work only. It must not import current legacy tasks or write a compatibility/dual-write bridge; BB-156 owns one-shot migration/cutover.

D9 — Decision publication is itself a CAS transaction. A JevDecision carries `observedGeneration`; publish rereads the current Work and applies the decision only when `observedGeneration === spec.generation` and the subject/attempt binding still matches. Otherwise publish returns `SUPERSEDED`, leaves phase/status unchanged, and never converts stale judgment into a current condition.
implementationSlices: S1 — Control authority + Work resource: implement CAS-backed dedicated-ref store and WORK_RESOURCE_V2 validation/generation semantics.
S2 — Executable lifecycle: implement phase/transition table, guards and deterministic `nextActions(work)`.
S3 — Pure context builder: derive phase-local agent context from Work/Attempt/decision facts with no persisted helper context.
S4 — Operator surface: add `bb-v2 create/show/next` commands that work identically from different source branches/worktrees.

S5 — Trust adapters/tests: bind synthetic Jev/Attempt/receipt facts to workGeneration and prove stale-generation/branch-split failures fail closed; document V2 as parallel, not yet authoritative for legacy work.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: One dedicated control authority returns identical Work state from different source checkouts and uses compare-and-swap publication. Claim/takeover lease expiry is decided by the ControlStore clock, never the agent clock.
evidenceRequired: Two checkout fixtures read the same control ref; stale CAS write is rejected.
Competing claims produce one winner; takeover before store-clock expiry is rejected; takeover after store-clock expiry advances the fence.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A new Work is created directly in V2 and can enter RESEARCHING without a source PR, legacy graph registration or source branch.
evidenceRequired: Create fixture proves no legacy graph/artifact write and returns a valid Work generation.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Current Work state deterministically yields legal next actions/blockers; `nextActions` is pure over `(spec,status,decisions)`; illegal transitions, stale observed generations and stale decision publication fail closed.
evidenceRequired: Table-driven transition tests cover research, judgment, execution, repair, merge-pending and delivered boundaries.
Independent controller instances over identical snapshots produce byte-equivalent next actions.
A decision whose observedGeneration differs from current spec.generation is SUPERSEDED and cannot mutate status/phase.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The V2 context builder is pure derived output with no persisted identity/history and exposes exact phase-local source authority and forbidden actions.
evidenceRequired: Repeated build is byte-equivalent and creates no context file; read-only phases expose no write scope.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Source branch/worktree/candidate state is only an Attempt bound to exact workId/workGeneration; claim/takeover uses store-clock CAS leases; fences protect only mutating attempt side effects and cannot redefine Work semantics.
evidenceRequired: Stale fence cannot publish candidate/evidence or transition state, while read-only show/context operations succeed without a fence.

invariantCoverage.invariant: Exactly one V2 control authority owns a Work's semantic/lifecycle state; source branches and worktrees cannot override it.
Work creation and research entry do not require a source-code commit or PR.
Context is always derived from Work + current system truth + exact decisions/attempt bindings and is never persisted as authority.
Every state transition is explicit, guarded and enumerable; no operator or agent infers lifecycle from prose.
Jev/evidence/delivery decisions remain external trusted receipts bound back to the exact Work generation and Attempt.

negativeVerificationCases: Changing the checked-out source branch changes `bb-v2 show` state for the same Work id, or competing agents both acquire the same live lease because agent clocks decide expiry.
A stale judgment/attempt bound to an older Work generation is published as current instead of returning SUPERSEDED, or two controllers derive different nextActions from the same canonical snapshot.
A stale fence mutates candidate/evidence/status, or read-only inspection/context building incorrectly requires a fence.

negativeCaseBindings.testTitle: BB-155 N1 ControlStore clock and CAS allow only one live attempt owner
BB-155 N2 stale decision is superseded and nextActions stays deterministic
BB-155 N3 fences guard mutations but never reads

livingDocs.statement: Living system state records the delivered V2 Blackboard control-plane boundary, dedicated authority, executable lifecycle and pure context-builder semantics while legacy work remains uncutover.
